en: Like it is important as well to have strong CICD patterns so that you can actually validate things with five minutes of effort and not 60 minutes or three hours of effort, making sure that you have good observability, making sure you have good testability, and not just, you know, empty calorie tests, but actual like real meaningful tests.
zh: 就像，拥有强大的 CICD 模式也很重要，这样你就可以用五分钟的工作量来真正验证东西，而不是 60 分钟或三个小时的工作量，确保你有好的可观测性，确保你有好的可测试性，而且不只是，你知道，空热量测试，而是真正的、有意义的测试。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones

en: If you are copying good practices, then you are going to have an easier time testing and validating what you're producing.

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: And that you know, starts with testing, starts with high quality comments.
zh: 而这，你知道，从测试开始，从高质量的注释开始。

zh: 即使是在我们的代码库里，我们的注释质量相对较高，我们也发现 AI 不幸地在那里把我们拉回了平均水平。

en: We're having like lots of very low low value comments that AI is creating, right?
zh: 我们出现了很多 AI 创造的非常低、低价值的注释，对吧？

zh: 就是说，那么你如何防范 AI 让你的代码库变糟？

zh: 你如何真正地传播围绕测试的好习惯、围绕可观测性的好习惯，确保我们以一种更容易把东西推上线到生产环境的方式来做工程？

zh: 而且，呃我想我们之前在节目外简短地聊过这个，但我们在这里给出的建议，其实和 AI 出现之前我们给出的建议是一样的，就是什么是功能正常的、什么是好的。

zh: 就是说，除了一点是，AI 已经让「吃蔬菜」这件事变得容易多了，只要你去让 AI 去做，而不是只是让 AI，你知道，胡乱编码一堆新功能塞进你的代码库，对吧？

en: Like you have a bunch of new engineering bandwidth.
zh: 就像，你有了一大批新的工程带宽。

zh: 而且因为机器永远不会感到无聊，让它们给你的代码库添加遥测(telemetry)是一件很棒的事情，对吧？

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Like to add rich Y events, to write to add attributes, right?
zh: 比如添加丰富的 Y 事件，去写、去添加属性，对吧？

zh: 就像，这些是我们过去不得不去告诉开发者的东西，你知道，就像让他们吃蔬菜或刷牙一样，对吧？

en: Is that did I get those numbers right?

en: And I think it really helps there to have a helpful assistant like Autobot, you know, pointing out problems so that the developer doesn't have to be a human linter or a human bug checker.
zh: 我认为在这方面有一个像 Autobot 这样的乐于助人的助手真的很有帮助,它帮你指出问题,这样开发者就不必做一个人肉代码检查器或人肉 bug 检查器。

zh: 问题在于,我们作为人类去验证正在生成的代码、正在提交的 pull request 的速度,验证它们是否有效、是否正确、是否经过了充分测试,正是如此,对吧?

en: Like I would argue any real production system should probably not be a dark factory, at least at this time.

zh: 我们要如何确保维持我们的标准?

zh: 而且我认为这些标准必须来自人类,对吧?

en: Like, I don't I don't think the robots are capable of coming up with enforcing the standards on their own, right?
zh: 就像,我不认为机器人有能力自己提出并执行标准,对吧?

en: Like we have to, right?
zh: 我们必须这么做,对吧?

en: Like, just because you have adaptive cruise control in your car doesn't mean that you can fully let go of the wheel, right?
zh: 就像,你的车里有了自适应巡航控制,并不意味着你可以完全放开方向盘,对吧?

speaker: Simon Maple
en: Like you still have to pay attention.

speaker: Simon Maple
en: It does sound very transformer-like, so it it it feels like it feels like we've got a lot of power on our side.

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Yeah, so originally we conceived of Autobots as this mechanism to automate the creation of small kind of bite-sized pull requests.
zh: 是的,最初我们把 Autobot 设想为一种自动化创建小型、一口大小的 pull request 的机制。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: And you know, we developed, we invested a fair amount of time in essentially doing clawed code in a box to work on a single linear ticket.
zh: 而且你知道,我们投入了相当多的时间,基本上是在做一个盒装版 clawed code,来处理单个线性工单。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: And it still does that, although we're in the process of sunsetting that because it turns out that now it's you know commoditized and now you can have bespoke services that do that in a box for you.
zh: 它现在仍然能做这件事,尽管我们正在逐步停用它,因为事实证明现在已经商品化了,现在你可以有定制化的服务在盒子里为你做这件事。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Um, but I think at the time when we started this effort in April or May, this was you know phenomenally effective in terms of for the first time having even developers who are not super fluent in clawed code be able to say, you know what?
zh: 嗯,不过我认为在我们四、五月份开始这项工作的时候,这是极其有效的,因为这是第一次,即使是那些对 clawed code 不太熟练的开发者也能说,你知道吗?

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: This this ticket looks relatively simple.
zh: 这个工单看起来相对简单。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: You know, nothing ventured, nothing gained, right?
zh: 你知道,不入虎穴焉得虎子,对吧?

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Like, you know, let's assign that ticket to Autobot and see what pull request it produces, right?
zh: 就像,你知道,我们把这个工单分配给 Autobot,看看它会产出什么样的 pull request,对吧?

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Um, so that's that's kind of how Autobot started.
zh: 嗯,这就是 Autobot 开始的方式。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Was it was this effort to kind of clear off the lower hanging fruit that doesn't require a developer to supervise and tell the robot consistently and steer it, right?
zh: 这是一种把那些较低垂的果实清理掉的努力,那些不需要开发者持续监督、告诉机器人并引导它的任务,对吧?

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Like, you know, this is the kind of design direction I want this to take.
zh: 就像,你知道,这是我希望它采取的设计方向。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: The theory was if you decomposed everything into a linear ticket well enough so that it would be able to, you know, complete the linear ticket on its own, that then your Autobot could take that and turn it into a pull request, and then you could, as a human who requested the Autobot to run, you could go ahead and and review that self-review first, and then after that hand that to your peer reviewer to to review as well.
zh: 当时的理论是,如果你把所有东西都充分分解成线性工单,让它能够独立完成那个线性工单,那么你的 Autobot 就可以接手并把它变成一个 pull request,然后你,作为请求 Autobot 运行的人类,可以先自己审查一遍,然后再把它交给你的同行评审去审查。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Um so that's how it started.
zh: 嗯,这就是它开始的方式。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: And then we realized that there were a relatively small percentage of these smaller tickets, and also that same functionality could also be used to reproduce kind of in a box the functionality that I think in April or March this year, uh Claude uh Anthropic released this Claude Code Reviews functionality.
zh: 然后我们意识到这类较小的工单占比相对较小,而且同样的功能也可以用来在盒子里复现一种功能——我认为在今年四月或三月,Claude 也就是 Anthropic 发布了 Claude Code Reviews 这个功能。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: And it was phenomenally expensive, it was like $20 or $30 per run, and it took like 10 or 20 minutes to run.
zh: 它极其昂贵,每次运行要 20 或 30 美元,而且要花 10 到 20 分钟才能跑完。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: And we looked at it and we said, actually, we want something like this.
zh: 我们看了之后说,实际上,我们想要类似这样的东西。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Um, but we would prefer that it be that it run within less than two or three minutes, that it costs dollars per pull request and not tens of dollars.
zh: 嗯,但我们更希望它在两三分钟内运行完成,成本是每个 pull request 几美元,而不是几十美元。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: Um so we pivoted the Autobots project towards handling reviews because we realized that our human developers were more than capable of creating this mass volume of pull requests anyways, Autobots or not.
zh: 嗯,所以我们把 Autobot 项目转向了处理审查,因为我们意识到我们的人类开发者无论如何都完全有能力创建这种大量的 pull request,不管有没有 Autobot。

speaker: Liz Fong-Jones
en: And that we needed to focus that instead on how do we make the review load over human reviewers uh lighter.
zh: 而我们需要把精力转而集中在如何减轻人类评审员的审查负担上。

speaker: Simon Maple
en: And and how does um so obviously, you know, Claude as a as a as an LLM or a general LLM, um, these types of things will always be kind of like very expensive uh and and long to run.
zh: 那么如何……显然,你知道,Claude 作为一个 LLM 或通用 LLM,嗯,这类东西运行起来总是非常昂贵而且耗时很长。

en: Uh in the news this week, so this will tell folks when we recorded it, uh obviously Jev is is making uh a lot of waves right now.

speaker: Simon Maple
en: It's hitting the it's hitting the headlines uh in most places.
zh: 它在大多数地方都登上了头条新闻。

en: Um with with an LLM which is very specific to kind of being able to provide you know yes-no answers or multiple choice, does that how how will that now impact uh places or or you know specific tasks like code review?
zh: 嗯,用一个非常适合提供是或否回答或选择题的 LLM,这会如何影响那些地方,或者说像代码审查这样的特定任务?

en: Yeah, so I think the primary place where we're thinking about deploying JEV right now is classifying pull requests into safe to merge with just the automatic review versus not safe to merge requires a human review.
zh: 是的,我认为我们目前考虑部署 JEV 的主要场景,是把 pull request 分类为:仅通过自动审查即可安全合并, versus 不安全合并、需要人工审查。
